title: Right Triangles and Trigonometry
subtitle: Master the Pythagorean theorem, SOH-CAH-TOA, and complementary angle identities

sections.title: The Right Triangle Foundation
sections.content:
In a right triangle with legs $a$, $b$ and hypotenuse $c$:
$$a^2 + b^2 = c^2 \quad \text{(Pythagorean Theorem)}$$

The three trigonometric ratios for an angle $\theta$:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}} \qquad \cos\theta = \frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}} \qquad \tan\theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}$$

**Memory trick: SOH-CAH-TOA**

sections.title: Type 1: Finding a Trig Ratio from a Triangle
Reading the Triangle
sections.content:
'Opposite' and 'adjacent' are always **relative to the angle** you're looking at.

For angle $\theta$:
- **Opposite:** the side across from $\theta$
- **Adjacent:** the side next to $\theta$ (not the hypotenuse)
- **Hypotenuse:** always the longest side, opposite the right angle

sections.problem: [IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: Right triangle with legs 35 and some value, hypotenuse 171. Angle at one vertex labeled.] What is $\sin$ of the labeled angle?

steps.description: Identify the opposite and hypotenuse relative to the angle

sections.tip: Always identify which vertex the angle is at, then label the opposite, adjacent, and hypotenuse relative to THAT angle.

sections.problem: [IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: Right triangle with one angle = θ, adjacent side = 4, hypotenuse unknown, one side = 3.] What is the hypotenuse?
sections.tip: Common Pythagorean triples: **3-4-5**, **5-12-13**, **8-15-17**, **7-24-25**. Memorize these to avoid calculation.

sections.title: sin and cos Are Complementary
sections.content:
In any right triangle, the two acute angles are complementary (they sum to $90°$).

This gives us a crucial identity:
$$\sin(\theta) = \cos(90° - \theta)$$
$$\cos(\theta) = \sin(90° - \theta)$$

In plain English: **the sine of an angle equals the cosine of its complement**.

On the SAT: if $\angle R + \angle S = 90°$, then $\sin R = \cos S$ (and vice versa).

sections.title: Example: sin equals cos of Complement
sections.problem: In right triangle $RST$, $\angle R + \angle S = 90°$. The value of $\sin R = \dfrac{\sqrt{15}}{4}$. What is $\cos S$?

steps.description: Since R and S are complementary: sin R = cos S

sections.tip: This identity is the single most tested trig fact on the SAT. Memorize: if two angles in a right triangle add to 90°, their sin and cos are swapped.

sections.title: Example: Identify the Equivalent Expression
sections.problem:
[IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: Right triangle with angles X and Y, where X + Y = 90°.]

Which expression is equivalent to $\cos X$?

steps.description: cos X = sin of the complementary angle

sections.title: Type 3: Similar Triangles and Trig Ratios
Trig Ratios Are Equal in Similar Triangles
sections.content:
If $\triangle FGH \sim \triangle JKL$ with $\angle F = \angle J$, then their trig ratios are identical:
$$\sin F = \sin J, \quad \cos F = \cos J, \quad \tan F = \tan J$$

This is because trig ratios depend only on the angle, not the size of the triangle.

sections.title: Example: Trig Ratios in Similar Triangles
sections.problem: Triangle $FGH$ is similar to triangle $JKL$ where $\angle F$ corresponds to $\angle J$. If $\sin F = \dfrac{308}{317}$, what is $\sin J$?

steps.description: Corresponding angles in similar triangles are equal, so their trig ratios are equal

sections.title: Type 4: Using Tangent to Find a Side
Example: Full Triangle from One Trig Ratio
sections.problem: In triangle $XYZ$, $\angle Z = 90°$, $YZ = 24$, and $\tan X = \dfrac{12}{35}$. What is the perimeter of $\triangle XYZ$?

steps.description: tan X = opposite/adjacent. Opposite to X is YZ = 24. So 24/XZ = 12/35
Find the hypotenuse XY using the Pythagorean theorem

sections.tip: tan X = 12/35 means the opposite-to-adjacent ratio is 12:35. Scale up: if opposite = 24, then adjacent = 70, hypotenuse = √(24²+70²) = 74 (a 12-35-37 triple scaled by 2).

sections.title: Type 5: Identifying the Trig Expression from a Triangle
Example: Match the Ratio to the Trig Function
sections.problem: [IMAGE PLACEHOLDER: Right triangle with sides 41, 42, and hypotenuse. Angle labeled X. The ratio 42/41 is shown.] Which trig function of which angle equals 42/41?

steps.description: Identify what 41 and 42 represent relative to each angle
steps.math: \text{If 42 is adjacent and 41 is opposite to angle X: } \tan X = \frac{41}{42}

steps.description: If the ratio is 42/41 with 42 as hypotenuse and 41 as opposite to angle Y: sin Y = 41/42

sections.answer: Match the ratio to SOH-CAH-TOA based on which sides are labeled relative to the angle.
sections.tip: Write 'opp', 'adj', 'hyp' next to each side label relative to the angle being asked about. Then apply SOH-CAH-TOA.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: **Similar triangles:** corresponding angles have equal trig ratios
**tan to find sides:** if $\tan X = k/m$, the opposite and adjacent are in ratio $k:m$

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Confusing opposite and adjacent (they depend on which angle you're looking at)
- Forgetting the complementary identity: $\sin R = \cos S$ when $R + S = 90°$
- Using the hypotenuse as the adjacent side
- Not scaling up a trig ratio properly to find actual side lengths

sat_tips: sin(θ) = cos(90° - θ): if two acute angles add to 90°, their sin and cos are swapped
Label every side as 'opp', 'adj', or 'hyp' relative to the angle BEFORE applying SOH-CAH-TOA
Memorize Pythagorean triples: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17 — they appear frequently
For similar triangles: trig ratios of corresponding angles are always equal
